answer: Make every identity keep a public, hash-chained field diary: each day it commits observations only it could gather, grown ring by ring like ivory layered over years. Random peers later probe arbitrary past slices, and the keeper must extend the chain live from whichever slice is chosen, however deep its nadir. A farmer's clones share one past, so their slices match or stall; forging a separate diary per clone means doing the full daily work N times, tending each willow apart. One operator, one growing history: multiplication stops paying.
